Introducing the next generation PLKB Gambit V2 - the ultimate all-around kite for every rider. This kite has been redesigned from the ground up to provide a better, more responsive flying experience with a range of new features and improvements.

Firstly, we've made some changes to the plan view, resulting in a lighter and faster steering experience with less bar pressure. The new profile provides better performance, stability and hangtime, allowing for more confidence when riding. Using Teijin materials on the leading edge and canopy, resulting in a more direct feeling with less stretch over the span.

The new Gambit V2 also has a more rounded tip for a better relaunch and is lighter, allowing it to fly in even less wind. We've adjusted the LE thickness for a lighter feel with less drag while ensuring stiffness is maintained where it matters. With fewer bridle lines, there's less drag and a shorter piece of unsheathed Dyneema line to keep the kite in better tune for longer.

But that's not all - the Gambit V2 also provides more lift, is better at looping, and is more versatile than ever before. This kite truly is an all-around performer, providing endless fun for riders of all skill levels, while larger one-pump valves and tubes make it easy to set up and inflate. Finally, Kevlar reinforcements on spots that get a lot of abrasions ensure that the Gambit V2 is built to last.

Whether you're just starting out or a seasoned pro, the PLKB Gambit V2 has everything you need to take your riding to the next level. With its new features and improvements, this kite is ready to help you tackle any challenge that comes your way.

With the Hook v4, we have achieved our goal of creating a kite that is not only powerful but also super comfortable to ride with an enormous wind range.

Focus on massive depower, higher flying speed, and exceptional stability in stormy conditions make this kite the perfect tool for taking your riding to the next level. Pulling on the bar will give you the massive boost you need to soar skyward.

Hook V4s' leading edge was further fine-tuned and updated with a new 4-point bridle system. With less drag through the air, this kite is quick and playful through its turns and is perfect for most conditions.

The new extended range now features 7.0 and 9.0 sizes allowing riders to utilize the perfect size depending on wind conditions and riders' personal preferences.

Each size of the Hook V4 has a unique design tailored to specific wind conditions. Sizes below 10 meters are designed for stronger winds, while 10 meters and up are optimized for lower wind speeds, creating more lift with lower speeds. As with any plane, the lift is generated by the wing profile and speed. Larger kites have less speed than smaller kites, which requires a different wing profile and shape to achieve maximum height.

Build to last, all Hook V4 sizes are made using super durable Teijin Triple Ripstop fabric and feature multiple Kevlar and Dacron reinforcements along its canopy and leading edge.

To inflate your PLKB LEI fast and effortless we offer you the PLKB Kite Pump 2.3L.

The pump offers 2 setting for easy inflation of your kite. Setting one is a double action (2 x 2300cc), which inflates your kite fast up to 8PSI. To go for that extra mile, reduce the effort needed to keep pumping at higher pressure, this way you can easily pump your kite to the max which in turn increases the performance of the kite. By switching to a single action you can pump effortless up to 13PSI.

The pump has comfortable grips and requires a lot less effort and it is suitable for kites of all sizes. The pump also features a pressure gauge and kite leash to attach your kite to.

We’re excited to present the all-new Nova V2! Be the first and last on the water, jump the highest or race up- or downwind, there is no Wing that can beat the fun with the Nova V2!

The new Nova has been redefined and offers a lot more than you could see at first sight. The Dynamic profile of the Nova ensures the perfect combination between stability and ease of use, while creating a superfast and agile foil with a massive depower range. The new Nova is made of Skytex 32 making it a very lightweight wing that flies even in the lightest breeze. Developed for foil riders that want maximum stability with only little wind, while progressing in speed and racing.

The Nova’s innovative Dynamic profile makes the kite adjustable across its entire depower reach. Depowering the Nova creates a full reflex profile for more stability and control. Powering the Nova will release something spectacular resulting in a superfast and agile wing.

Every size has been developed individually to maximize performance. Each size comes with a different Aspect Ratio, Cell count and profile. This year we also introduce the 15- and 18-meter ‘SuperNova’. These performance wings were developed with more race behavior for foil- and buggy riders in mind.

The Nova has been thoroughly tested, in many different conditions; on Twin-tips, by Foil riders, Buggy riders and even on ski’s in a 2000km endurance trip in the Artic circle by Eric Leegwater, all to make sure that you get the best. A versatile and intuitive wing that makes you want to Never Stop Playing.

The Nova is made of durable Skytex 32 and with a weight starting at 1.11 kg, it gets you up on the water with only a few knots. The one-way inlets were redesigned to create an even more airtight foil that makes water relaunches effortless, even in low wind conditions.

The new Nova V2 is a super versatile kite that you can easily fly as an Lei kite while enjoying all benefits of a Foil kite at the same time; small packing, large wind range, huge big air and a competitive top speed.

The Nova has been thoroughly tested, in many different conditions; on Twin-tips, by Foil riders, Buggy riders and even on ski’s in a 2000km endurance trip in the Artic circle by Eric Leegwater, all to make sure that you get the best. A versatile and intuitive wing that makes you want to Never Stop Playing.

Description:
With over 20 years of continuous evolution, the Purelip has become the benchmark for uncompromising wave performance. Built to thrive in the most demanding conditions, it excels in waves, bump blasting, and big days.

The 2026 Purelip brings fresh refinements to this proven formula. The Exocet RF V4 range excels in light breezes and high-powered conditions without compromising control or comfort. Engineered for speed foiling, the boards feature an optimized aerodynamic deck and bottom.

The lineup offers two distinct shapes – the 75 and 85 – each focused on the high-speed capabilities of hydrofoils, ensuring efficient airflow while in flight. The front rails are shaped thinner, with a generous tuck along the bottom and a subtly domed deck. This design refines airflow, slicing through the wind and reducing resistance.

The rail and deck shape significantly reduce overall volume, aligning them closely with the sleek profiles of fin slalom boards of the same width. This minimized volume aids in sinking the tail during pumping, allowing the foil to load swiftly for nearly instantaneous take-off. Twin parallel cut-outs further enhance board momentum, boosting take-off efficiency.

In the case of a touchdown, particularly at high speeds, the rail tuck paired with twin parallel cut-outs shrinks the wetted surface of the bottom, reducing drag and deceleration. This gives the rider valuable time to regain control and stabilize the flight with precision.

A wide tail enables footstraps to be positioned farther from the board’s centerline, offering enhanced leverage to fine-tune foil pitch with greater accuracy while improving upwind tracking. Conversely, positioning the footstraps more inboard provides tighter control of foil pitch when navigating downwind.

The RF V4 is an evolutionary step from the slower, more forgiving freefoil boards. Their direct feedback and explosive character quickly become indispensable once the transition is made.

The RPM is dedicated to pure freeride windsurfing and comes with all the benefits of inflatable construction. It is an accessible board that brings fun and excitement to all rider levels – beginner to advanced.

With ample volume, the RPM iWindsurf is forgiving for novices who are taking their first steps. When not planing, the board can be fitted with the centre fin to limit sideways drift and track better upwind.

Its compact hull shape ensures early planning and the rail curves have been optimised for turns and gybes. The inflatable construction – highly resistant to damage from catapult falls –prevents costly dings and allows advanced sailors to fully concentrate on their sailing. A sharp PVC edge runs along the rails and tail of the board. This feature greatly improves water release, reduces drag, and improves the planing capabilities of the board.

The RPM iWindsurf uses diamond-pattern and directional-groove EVA deck padding to ensure the rider has an optimal grip at all times.

Unifiber Comfort Footstraps are supplied. These are bolted into the embedded inserts and provide the rider with maximum comfort and control.

Inflatable construction makes the RPM iWindsurf easy to store and transport.

Two construction options are available: The Single Layer version can be pumped to 15 psi. These are light weight and well-made boards with standard performance. The Fusion Composite Dropstitch version can be pumped to 20 psi. These boards have a more direct feel and are super stiff for the best possible performance.
Pro #1: To prevent possible damage do not use excessive force to roll up your board, and do not put any weight onto the rolled-up board in storage
Pro #2: Use a Cardan type baseplate to connect a windsurf rig

The RDM iWindsurf board is made using a fusion composite dropstitch. Boards in this technology can sustain high pressure (up to 20 psi) while remaining light and durable.

The RPM is dedicated to pure freeride windsurfing and comes with all the benefits of inflatable construction. It is an accessible board that brings fun and excitement to all rider levels – beginner to advanced.

With ample volume, the RPM iWindsurf is forgiving for novices who are taking their first steps. When not planing, the board can be fitted with the centre fin to limit sideways drift and track better upwind.

Its compact hull shape ensures early planning and the rail curves have been optimised for turns and gybes. The inflatable construction – highly resistant to damage from catapult falls –prevents costly dings and allows advanced sailors to fully concentrate on their sailing. A sharp PVC edge runs along the rails and tail of the board. This feature greatly improves water release, reduces drag, and improves the planing capabilities of the board.

The RPM iWindsurf uses diamond-pattern and directional-groove EVA deck padding to ensure the rider has an optimal grip at all times.

Unifiber Comfort Footstraps are supplied. These are bolted into the embedded inserts and provide the rider with maximum comfort and control.

Inflatable construction makes the RPM iWindsurf easy to store and transport.

Two construction options are available: The Single Layer version can be pumped to 15 psi. These are light weight and well-made boards with standard performance. The Fusion Composite Dropstitch version can be pumped to 20 psi. These boards have a more direct feel and are super stiff for the best possible performance.
Pro #1: To prevent possible damage do not use excessive force to roll up your board, and do not put any weight onto the rolled-up board in storage
Pro #2: Use a Cardan type baseplate to connect a windsurf rig

The new RS designs are purpose-built boards designed to meet the rigorous standards of PWA slalom events, ensuring top performance in all conditions.

Each shape has been optimized and tested for a specific wind range to deliver an exceptional performance regardless of the conditions.

To keep the racer's focus on maintaining speed through the course, all outlines have undergone through subtle tweaks to exercise control even when conditions get rough. These refinements, such as reducing the outline curve near the front foot area and introducing a more pronounced V-shape on the bottom from the back foot to the mast track, provide enhanced control even in challenging conditions.

Volume had been redistributed in the footstraps area allowing riders to adopt a more locked-in stance. Alongside this, the reduction in rail thickness in the nose area provides the RS boards with a superb grip in the gybes, allowing you to maintain a competitive edge on the course

While these boards offer outstanding slalom performance, we have also incorporated Exocet's DNA by integrating DDSA (double-density shock absorbers), which provide much-needed comfort and control, vital elements for both PWA races and long-distance sailing.

The hull plan has been reimagined and updated, including adjustments to the outline and volume distribution. Tail cutouts had been removed to prioritize control over the release in stormy small sail heats. Overall, this board is perfect for high-wind conditions, whether on flat water or in challenging conditions, providing absolute comfort and confidence.

Given that most sailing days, whether recreational or competitive, feature winds below 15 knots, the primary challenge addressed by the RS V5 AST 380 is creating a board that is both accessible and effective for sailors of all skill levels.

The RS V5 AST 380 raceboard aims to provide an easy-to-handle, cost-effective solution that still delivers competitive performance, ensuring optimal sailing experiences for novices and experienced sailors alike in light to medium wind conditions.

Instead of using an expensive carbon layup, the robust body of the RS V5 AST 380 is constructed with a monolithic build and full-wrap fiberglass rail band reinforcements to maintain necessary rigidity. Several T-stringers are introduced to preserve a fair amount of stiffness.

The nose of the board features a "scow" design, which helps prevent it from digging into the water when sailing upwind on the rail. This design also extends the board's straight outline further forward, which is crucial for maximizing performance in light wind conditions.

Opting for a pin tail makes the hull significantly more effective on the upwind course. While the lack of tail width might seem to hamper the RS V5 AST 380's reaching and downwind performance, positioning the fin significantly forward ensures the board maintains perfect "power" during these legs, providing the necessary drive and control.

Overall, the thoughtful design and features of the RS V5 AST 380 raceboard make it a versatile and effective choice for light to medium wind sailing, catering to a wide range of sailors and sailing conditions.

The RS V5 AST 380 is registered with ISAF.

The RS V5 Carbon 380 from Exocet stands out as the most advanced and tactical design in their range, exclusively dedicated to raceboarding.

In the quest for victory on the race course, every detail matters. Sailors must be prepared to excel in various conditions, from marginal winds to strong gusts and challenging waters. They need the ability to fine-tune and adjust their equipment on the fly, maximizing every bit of wind available.

The RS V5 Carbon 380 is specifically engineered to provide racers with the essential tools to gain an advantage within the fleet.

Significant improvements have been made to the board, particularly in reaching and sailing close-hauled. The daggerboard and mast track have been slightly repositioned forward, enhancing the board's sensitivity and getting on a rail quicker in lighter and marginal winds.

The tail section has undergone modifications, incorporating a light V design to enhance course stability and navigation in choppy waters. This update also offers improved release during reaching. Combined with the readjusted fins position, this synergy generates enhanced grip and power when planing.

The daggerboard has been further fine-tuned to optimize its weight and effectiveness on the race course.

While the RS V5 Carbon 380 is primarily designed as a tactical racing board, it doesn't compromise on fun and performance for recreational use.

Description:
Designed as a dedicated slalom machine, the RS design undergoes constant development and fine-tuning by Partice and his test team, ensuring top-notch performance on the race course.

To maintain the racer's focus on maintaining speed throughout the course, subtle adjustments have been made to all outlines to enhance control even in rough conditions. Notably, the widest point of the board has been shifted closer to the nose while maintaining the same tail width. This refinement flattens the outline curve, significantly improving control on straight lines and allowing to approach gybes with greater speed.

The bottom shape features a mono concave beneath the nose that transitions into a consistent V shape from underneath the mast track to the back foot. This configuration aids in sustaining speed and direction even when facing challenging choppy conditions.

In the footstraps area, deck thickness has been reduced to re-balance front and back foot positions. With a new setup, the front foot will feel less "loose" in rough conditions. Alongside this, the slight increase in rail thickness in the nose area boosts the early planing capability of the RS design and improves control during gybes.

While these boards offer outstanding slalom performance, we have also incorporated Exocet's DNA by integrating DDSA (double-density shock absorbers), which provide much-needed comfort and control, vital elements for both PWA races and long-distance sailing.

Notably, the RS 58 boasts a distinct shape within the RS range, drawing inspiration from the renowned Exocet Turboboost 58. The hull plan has been thoughtfully reimagined and updated, involving adjustments to the outline and volume distribution. Tail cutouts have been omitted, prioritizing control over release during turbulent small sail heats. Overall, this board is an ideal choice for high-wind conditions, whether it's on flat water or in challenging environments, providing unparalleled comfort and confidence.

Built for the pure pursuit of slalom speed, the RS V6 channels decades of design expertise and countless hours on the racecourse. Every line, rail, and contour is there to help you accelerate sooner, carve faster, and stay in control when it matters most.

The outline is tuned to balance stability and drive. With the widest point moved forward and the tail held wide, the RS V6 holds a steady track across gusts and chop, letting you stay focused on your line and approach gybes without hesitation.

Underfoot, the bottom shape transitions from a mono concave in the nose to a continuous V through the rear. This combination smooths out rough water and keeps the board locked in, even when you’re pressing for maximum speed.

Deck thickness is reduced around the footstraps to keep your stance connected and natural. The subtle rebalancing of foot pressure helps the front foot feel planted through aggressive reaches and turbulent patches. At the nose, slightly thicker rails lift early onto the plane and stay composed in tight corners.

Every RS V6 includes Exocet’s hallmark double-density shock absorbers under the footstraps, which deliver crucial comfort and control across long races and demanding training days.

Among the range, the RS 58 carries a character all its own. Inspired by the Exocet’s classic Turboboost 58, it trades tail cutouts for a clean outline that favours consistent control over raw release. Whether you’re racing in high winds on flat water or navigating gusty courses, it’s a board that rewards committed riding with confidence and comfort.

Developed by Exocet’s raceboard team featuring, Marcos Ruesch, Curro Manchon, and Patrice Belbeoc’h, the RS V7 represents one of the most advanced and tactical designs in the range. For sailors competing in diverse conditions, it offers the tools needed to navigate challenging courses and make the most of every breath of wind.

Building on the proven success of earlier concepts such as the Unifiber Proteus hull, the focus has been on refining construction methods and shape to create a board capable of exceptional upwind speed without compromising downwind and reaching performance.

The hull is carefully balanced by a low profile and generous volume distribution at the bow and stern, preserving total volume while improving stability and trim. Where earlier designs often favoured heavier sailors upwind and lighter sailors downwind, the RS V7 accommodates a wide weight range, helping heavier sailors plane early and giving lighter sailors better control upwind.

The daggerboard retains the effective Pivot System, allowing adjustments to length and angle to suit conditions. A longer blade delivers extra power on light-wind upwind legs or can be retracted for control in stronger breezes. The housing is designed to accept custom setups, and both the daggerboard and mast track are positioned forward to optimise balance.

A subtle shift of the fin box forward enhances drive when reaching, rounding out a set of features aimed at all-around performance across every leg of the racecourse.

Developed and refined by committed sailors, the RS V7 is a raceboard built for those who demand precision and adaptability in any condition.

The Raceboardblade OD integrates the extensive experience and development of the Loftsails raceboard team, delivering performance in light to medium wind conditions for both novice and experienced sailors in a competitive, cost-effective design.

Based on the Loftsails Raceboardblade ULW range, the Raceboardblade OD retains the key profile and design elements that made the original so successful on the racecourse. Available in 6.5, 7.5, and 8.5 sizes, the Raceboardblade OD mirrors the ULW range with optimized vertical curves, horizontal shapes, and leech release for excellent upwind and downwind capabilities.

The main window and upper body have been modified to include monofilm panels. The profile is stabilized by a 3-cam and a 5 fiberglass rod and tube battens setup, creating a super light frame that is particularly suited for lighter winds and offers excellent pumping response.

The OD mast pocket is constructed using different materials: the upper part is made of dacron, while the lower pocket is cut from SU250. It features the original Blade mast pocket design, which includes three layers (two pocket sides and an interior mast panel) all tensioned by the downhaul. This unique Loftsails design equalizes downhaul tension between the mast panel and mast pocket, resulting in a firm, easy-rotating leading edge

All sizes feature Loftsails’ signature trim sensitivity within their respective wind ranges, ensuring maximum performance and responsiveness.

Central to the Loftsails racing program, Racingblade is a purpose-built sail engineered for maximum efficiency with fin setups. Specifically developed for competitive slalom racing, it meets all PWA rules and regulations while delivering the acceleration and top-end speed serious racers demand.

The 2026 Racingblade continues its legacy of continuous refinement, introducing a series of updates that elevate handling and performance. Subtle batten angle re-orientation and re-scheduled luff curves improve balance and lower the sail’s center of gravity, while a slightly lower foot profile increases control and delivers even more drive when powered up. The higher aspect ratio and revised shaping reduce drag and create a locked-in, aerodynamic feel across a broad wind range.

At the heart of the Racingblade’s stability are carefully tuned battens, combining longer rod sections and rear-shifted tube segments to create a shallower entry profile. This configuration further cuts drag and promotes smoother, quicker cam rotation. All battens are housed in side-alternating X-Ply pockets to minimize asymmetry and preserve a clean, stable shape under the load. For 2026 Racingblades are equipped with the new 30% lighter Loftsails TekCam 3 system that further enhances cam rotation and accommodates higher batten angles, supporting the sail’s refined shaping without sacrificing smooth rigging or handling.

The mast pocket uses 2-mil quad-axial X-Ply and IYU250 woven material to create a double-layer stretch-resistant zone. This zone runs from head to tack just behind the mast, helping the pocket maintain its precise shape over time. To further improve durability, the mast sleeve now features a 50mm triple-sewn seam, resisting wear through years of rigging and racing.

The new Dual Kevlar clew radials stabilize the sail’s profile under heavy load, distributing forces more evenly and supporting consistent drive and forward pull. Reinforcements across the central window, leech, and foot panels use X-Ply laminates, while 4.0 mil bi-ply body panels provide excellent UV and stretch resistance. For 2026, 5.0 mil foot panels increase durability in high-wear zones, ensuring long-lasting performance session after session.

Finished in a clean, functional minimalism graphic, the Racingblade sheds unnecessary marker cloth and scrim, reducing visual clutter while also lowering the sail’s weight center. The result is a more balanced feel and enhanced reactivity in all conditions.

The Racingblade 2026 is a refined tool built to extract every knot of speed, every ounce of control, and every advantage when it matters most.

Racingblade is Loftsails' dedicated, no-compromise slalom racing design, meticulously crafted to meet the demands of competitive slalom racing.

The design of Racingblade has undergone continuous refinement since its inception in 2007, with the Loftsails testing team working tirelessly to perfect its performance.

The sail features an efficient and stable profile with a free-twisting leech and a low-drag wide mast pocket. To ensure an effective leading edge, the wide mast pocket requires firm tension. Racingblade tackles this challenge with a unique pocket construction. The webbing of the downhaul roller is attached not only to the main mast panel but to both mast pocket sides as well, equalizing the loading and resulting in a firm, clean, and easily rotating leading edge.

The upper part of the sail is slightly narrower. In combination with a tighter middle section of the leech, this creates a crisper and stiffer sail with a more direct feel. The adjusted luff curves and revised batten shapes optimize the forward-oriented profile, improving acceleration and facilitating smoother and quicker cam rotation.

In challenging conditions, every detail matters. Regular batten pockets can cause profile asymmetry, but Racingblade incorporates x-ply batten pockets to maintain profile stability through gusts and lulls on both sides.

Durability is a key feature of all Loftsails designs, and Racingblade is no exception. The construction includes x-ply panels for the central window, leech, and foot, along with bi-ply top panels that offer extreme UV resistance.

Even under massive loads and extensive wear and tear, Racingblade remains an uncompromising slalom design that delivers seasons of top-level performance.

The XO Sails x Unifiber hardware packs create a complete rigging ecosystem for the Rookie, Swing, Experience TR, Maverick, and Vega. All sail models of the same size fit the same mast and boom, making the system simple, flexible, and efficient. Each pack includes a mast, boom, base, and uphaul, pre-sorted in a convenient bag to keep everything together and easy to handle.

Ideal for schools, centres, and rentals, the system provides maximum flexibility: if a rig component breaks or goes missing, it can be substituted or replaced without affecting the rest of the setup. The uniform sizing also makes storage and shipping more efficient.

For sails from 1.0 to 2.5 square metres, packs are available with either aluminium or epoxy masts, while all larger packs use epoxy for increased durability and performance.

In sizes 4.5 and 5.5, a Compact Rig Pack is also available. Featuring a four-piece mast, three-piece boom, and carry bag, it fits any sail model but is particularly suited to the Swing, as its foldable sail design makes full use of the compact storage.

Our Scross range represents the latest generation of freerace boards developed by Exocet.

When you're seeking a slalom board that excels on the course but is comfortable to ride, the Scross is the perfect choice.

We have completely redesigned the lineup, introducing new shapes that offer a compact outline and a reworked hull. These boards feature an added V under the straps, allowing for early planing and a lively feel underfoot.

The central part of the deck surrounding the mast track is lowered. Recessing the mast track and lowering an entire rig helps to significantly boost control, even in challenging conditions.

The Scross Carbon version was developed for riders seeking heightened performance but without the excessive technicality of a full slalom board.

Additionally, the fin box was reinforced making the Scross foil compatible.
Pro #1: FOIL COMPATIBLE
Pro #2: FIN OPTIONS

Description:
The Scross V3 Silver range embodies Exocet’s commitment to accessible freerace sailing. For riders who appreciate the thrill of slalom speeds combined with dependable control, the Scross V3 offers a well-balanced platform.

A compact outline works in tandem with the refined hull shape to enhance quick planing and a responsive feel underfoot. Under the strap area, a V-shaped bottom helps the board release cleanly and rapidly reach cruising speed.

Control remains a priority. The deck around the mast track sits lower, reducing the rig’s centre of gravity and enhancing stability across changing conditions.

As with the majority of Exocet’s fin boards, the Scross V3 features double density shock absorbers. Positioned beneath the rider's feet when secured in the footstraps, the shock absorbers are designed to offer heightened comfort during challenging conditions.

The Scross V3 is ideal for those looking to unlock speed, responsive handling, and comfort without stepping into the demands of a full slalom board.

Description:
Protect your hydrofoil from galvanic corrosion!

Commonly affected are the bolts holding foil parts together. When stainless steel, titanium or carbon make contact with aluminium, it causes a reaction that can practically weld them together. Over time, materials can become brittle and break.

Isolating and water-repelling properties of the Shield Gel create a barrier between bolts and the aluminum, inhibiting the corroding process.

The Gel also lubricates, making foil assembly or disassembly quicker and easier.

Description:
The Skyblade sail is an extension of Loftsails' racing program, developed to maximize the performance of low-drag hydrofoils. This advanced design is tailored for competitive racing and fully adheres to PWA rules.

The Skyblade's design objective is top speed and control during flight. It features radically high aspect ratios and notably wide mast pockets, both contributing to balance and comfort in flight mode. The sail also incorporates a lower foot, reduced vertical shaping, and more aggressive batten angles, which enhance aerodynamics and provide the rig with exceptional stability.

The wide mast pockets require firm tension to maintain efficient airflow. Drawing inspiration from the Racingblade fin slalom program, the Skyblade adopts its unique mast pocket construction. Skyblade mast pockets are constructed with multiple laminate & woven panels. A double-layer stretch-resistance zone is formed with 2-mil quad-axial x-ply (a lightweight material that resists folding memory) and IYU250 woven mast pocket material. This integrated 2-ply tendon extends from head to tack just behind the mast and helps the mast pocket maintain its optimal condition over time.

The downhaul roller is attached to three layers: the two mast pocket sides and the mast pane in between. This setup evenly distributes downhaul loading to all three layers, resulting in a firm, clean, smooth-rotating leading edge. Smooth cam rotation is crucial for maintaining focus during races and provides the balance needed for smooth gybes and transitions.

High trim tension and extreme conditions can take a toll on sail performance over time. To counteract this, the Skyblade is equipped with Metallic Cam Interfaces at all camber inducer contact points, preventing material degradation and ensuring long-lasting performance.
Additionally, all Skyblades are manufactured with Loftsails' signature focus on material durability. The central window, leech, and foot feature x-ply panels, while the bi-ply top panels offer exceptional catastrophic failure and UV resistance, ensuring sail longevity.

All new Skyblades come with one camber set. Sizes 5.0 and smaller include TekCam2 RDM, while sizes 6.0 and larger come with TekCam2 SDM.
Pro #1: Cam Types: TekCam2 RDM are included with sizes 5.0 and smaller; TekCam2 SDM are included with sizes 6.0 and bigger.

Description:
Developed specifically to extract maximum performance from low-drag hydrofoils, the Skyblade’s design objectives are straightforward: top speed and total control in flight.

Radically high aspect ratios and wide mast pockets combine to create a rig that feels balanced and predictable in flight. For 2026, refinements across nearly every detail elevate this platform even further. Re-scheduled luff curves and slight batten angle re-orientation improve balance and lower the sail’s centers of effort and weight, while a lower foot with a shorter foot batten adds more efficient aerodynamics and control when fully powered.

At the center of the sail’s stability are the Skyblade’s carefully tuned carbon battens, which create a clean, light, locked-in profile with minimal drag. The new TekCam 3 camber system is 30% lighter and accommodates higher batten angles and ensures smooth, precise rotation. This reliable rotation is essential for maintaining focus during races and allows confident gybes and transitions without compromise.

The Skyblade’s mast pocket combines multiple laminate and woven panels in a double-layer stretch-resistant zone, built with 2-mil quad-axial X-Ply and IYU250 woven material. This integrated two-ply tendon extends from head to tack behind the mast, helping the pocket maintain optimal shape over time. A new 50mm triple-sewn mast sleeve seam further improves resistance to wear, season after season.

The addition of dual Kevlar 5.0 mil laminate clew radials stabilizes the sail under load and distributes forces evenly for reliable drive and forward pull.

To withstand the rigors of high tension and extreme loads, all camber inducer contact points are equipped with Metallic Cam Interfaces, preventing material degradation and ensuring consistent performance.

The Skyblade is constructed to deliver unmatched durability in competitive conditions. Reinforcements across the central window, leech, and foot feature X-Ply laminates, while bi-ply upper body panels provide outstanding UV resistance and catastrophic failure prevention. New 5mil X-ply laminate foot panels further enhance strength in critical wear zones.

Finished in a clean, functional minimalism graphic, the design sheds excess marker cloth and scrim to reduce swing weight and keep the center of weight lower.

The Skyblade 2026 is a dedicated foiling machine, ready to help you unlock more speed, more control, and more confidence in every race.

Skyscape, the personal choice of Loftsails' chief sail designer Monty Spindler, is a sail designed to provide versatility, lightness, and pure enjoyment in freefoil sailing.

With its high-aspect design, Skyscape perfectly balances the low drag of the hydrofoil. It features a shorter boom and no cams, allowing for effortless flipping during transitions without disrupting the board's delicate trim.

The current range of Skyscape sails has been expanded with the addition of new sizes: 4.2 and 4.7. These sizes are shaped with a 5-batten profile, while the other sizes maintain their stable 6-batten layout. Selected battens in each size have been revised and fine-tuned to create a more forward-oriented profile.

Skyscape sails offer a wide range of trimming options thanks to their strong luff curve and finely-tuned horizontal shapes. The double clew eyelets provide additional versatility, allowing the selected size to continue performing when others may need to change their sails.

Moreover, if foiling becomes less exciting, Skyscape sails can still be highly effective with a fin setup.

Similar to other Loftsails designs, all sail sizes below 7.0 are compatible with both RDM and SDM masts.

The display is made to the tenth of a unit up to 99.9, then to the unit. The aluminium base gives the camera great strength and the thread (1/4″) under the camera allows it to be attached to a photo tripod.

A larger and more robust anemometer, the Eole is equipped with a multi-directional propeller allowing a precise measurement without having to be perfectly oriented in the wind axis. It is the ideal companion for kite surfers or navigators.

The Eole is an unsinkable device, so it can fall into the water without disappearing into the abyss and its backlighting allows use even in reduced natural light.

The Swing V2 sail is designed for schools and centres looking to introduce beginners to windsurfing in a simple, dependable way. With its deep, forgiving profile, it offers clear feedback between power and depower, helping newcomers quickly understand balance, wind direction, and sail control.

Constructed from durable Dacron with a robust PVC window, the Swing V2 stands up to frequent use and everyday wear-and-tear. Diagonally cut sail foot allows the rig to move freely over the board, making it easier for learners to steer and manoeuvre larger boards.

Each size is colour-coded for fast identification on the water, so instructors and students can easily recognise which sail belongs to which rider.

Compared to the Experience TR rig, the Swing V2 is lighter, simpler, and especially well-suited to lighter winds and early sessions. Its classic shape places the centre of effort further back, giving clear, intuitive feedback but requiring more care in stronger or gusty conditions.

With minimal downhaul tension and straightforward rigging, the Swing V2 makes it easy for schools and clubs to get beginners on the water quickly and help them build confidence from day one.

Description:
Very few sails can enjoy their pedigree for as long as the Loftsails Switchblade.

Adopting the performance-based Racingblade design into a more approachable freerace 3-cam profile, Switchblade is a fast-paced sail with relentless acceleration and a massive tunning range. Sail is equipped with tube batten systems that are usually reserved for competitive designs and enhance control and stability at an upper end.

The Switchblade range is available in two construction variants. A standard option comes built with 3.5 mil exterior panels, monofilm central window, and bi-ply upper body panels. The HD version utilizes the same 3.5 mil exterior panels but replaces monofilm and bi-ply pan to 4 mil xply central window and 2 mil quad-axial upper body panels.

Being the first sail in its class to be tested on RDM mast and receiving glowing reviews, all Switchblade sizes (up to 7.8) are supplied with both RDM and SMD TekCam II cams.

Designed with speed and longevity in mind, Switchblade is freerace engine that will continue to thrill through years of service.

Few sails can claim a legacy as enduring as the Loftsails Switchblade. Born from the high-performance DNA of the Racingblade, the Switchblade channels that pedigree into a more approachable freerace 3-cam profile that delivers relentless acceleration and effortless speed.

For 2026, the Switchblade evolves with a host of refinements that sharpen its performance and durability. A higher aspect ratio with shorter booms creates a lighter, more agile feel, while re-scheduled luff curves and batten angle re-orientation improve balance and lower the sail’s centers of effort and weight. The updated slimmer profile shaping and a slightly lower foot add even more drive when powered up, making the sail feel locked in and efficient across a wide wind range.

At the heart of the Switchblade’s stability are tubed battens, proven to deliver the stiffness and reflex typically reserved for competitive racing designs. The new 30% lighter TekCam 3 system further enhances cam rotation and accommodates higher batten angles, supporting the sail’s refined shaping without sacrificing smooth rigging or handling.

Durability steps up to another level for 2026. New 5 mil foot panels and a reinforced 50mm triple-sewn mast sleeve seam withstand years of hard-charging freerace sessions. Description:
The brand new TECHNO FOIL is the ideal board for experiencing and enjoying freeride and foil-board riding. Conceived to do both to a high level, it enables you to sail in much lighter winds, and to get maximum fun in the widest range of conditions possible. With the foil, it's perfectly balanced and will have you sailing in as little as 10 knots of wind. The foil is wide, making it easy to get up, and to enjoy effortless control of the board itself. Remove the foil and you have a TECHNO that is powerful and very quickly up to planing, extremely responsive and high speed.

In this configuration, you'll get the best out of it between 15 and 25 knots of wind. It's a "convertible" package that will please riders who want the best of both, light-wind foil riding and strong-wind fun. The Techno Wind Foil is 100% Made-in-France using the BIC Sport exclusive ACE-TEC construction technology, resulting in a board with an unrivaled strength/weight ratio. The board was designed by one of the hottest shapers around, Jean-Marie Guiriec.

To maximize the performance in upwind and downwind sailing conditions, the Techno Wind Foil has to be trimmed correctly.

Note:The board may have minor imperfections in the graphic application. The structural integrity of the board and its performance are not affected.

The top part of the Baseplate Tendon Joint Cardan HD (U-Pin) V2.

Its cardan hinge allows effortless sail attachment on the beach or in the water, eliminating the need to flip the board or bend the tendon manually.

At the centre, a high-quality TPU tendon is secured with two large-diameter custom bolts, designed for easy replacement and to prevent over-torquing.

All metal components are made from stainless steel, ensuring a solid connection and long-lasting durability. For added safety, the parts are connected with a Spectra safety rope, capable of withstanding up to 650 kg of a breakload.

The cardan hinge design is particularly suitable for wind foilers, beginners, and inflatable windsurfing boards. It simplifies rigging and reduces strain on components. However, the tendon may deform slightly when used in combination with high-performance rigs.

Its top-grade TPU tendon core can be disassembled and replaced by hand, allowing you to inspect the tendon anytime and anywhere. The POK plastic caps secure the tendon pins. They snap into place easily, but cannot be moved while the baseplate is connected to the board/mast extension. You'll never be surprised by a broken tendon!

All metal components are manufactured from stainless steel, guaranteeing a solid connection and lasting durability.

The Tendon Joint Raceboard UF Essentials (U-pin) is designed to be compatible with Unifiber Proteus V1 and V2, as well as the Starboard Phantom 2021 and newer models.

Simple and reliable, the tendon joint sits very low, creating a more direct connection between the rig and the board, which makes it easier to "close the gap." At its core is a high-quality TPU tendon, secured by two large-diameter custom bolts for easy tendon replacement without bolt overturning.

The U-Pin section on top is made from a single solid piece of stainless steel, ensuring lasting durability. Despite its strength, the Raceboard UF tendon joint is light, weighing approximately 50g less than competing products.

To ensure smooth movement over the mast track, the tendon joint features a high-grade nylon pad that is ergonomically shaped to securely lock the joint to the carriage without hindering its movement.

For added safety, the top and bottom parts of the tendon joint are connected with a Spectra safety rope, capable of withstanding up to 650 kg of break load.
Pro #1: The tendon joint is compatible with Unifiber Proteus V1-V2, Starboard Phantom 2021 and newer

Description:
The Vega V2 is a versatile performance sail designed to deliver high-end handling and dependable durability without stretching your budget. Whether you’re carving waves, enjoying lively bump & jump sessions, or chasing freeride speed across flat water, the Vega adapts to match your style.

Each size is tuned for specific conditions, with four battens in the smallest sails for manoeuvrability, five battens in medium sizes for balanced control, and six battens plus a crossbatten cut-out in the largest sails to maintain a stable, powerful profile. Tapered battens help create a clean shape that stays responsive as the wind builds.

Constructed from a combination of white bi-ply, 4 mil X-ply, and a full X-ply window, the Vega offers solid UV resistance and reliable strength for regular use. Mast foot protection keeps your deck and your feet safe, while downhaul pulleys make rigging smooth and efficient.

To get the most out of the Vega V2’s performance potential, the sail is paired with Unifiber original constant curve masts and booms to deliver optimal response and early planing. For a more cost-effective setup, the sail is also compatible with Unifiber x XOsails rig packs.

The Wavescape’s head panels use dual-layer Dacron to improve roll-up ease and enhance long-term durability.

Loftsails Standing Batten technology provides optimized forward-oriented drive without compromising resilience in the waves.

From abrasion-resistant mast pads to strategically placed PVC protectors, every detail is engineered to withstand season after season of committed riding.

Description:
The core principle behind Exocets' Windsup is less time on the beach and more fun on the water.

With its distinctive drop-like shape, inspired by surf longboards, the Windsup works is an exceptional platform for recreational water sports. Whether it's stand-up paddleboarding (SUP), windsurfing, or even wind foiling, the setup is yours to choose from.

Step tail is a very distinct design feature. It gives the board excellent glide capabilities in sub-planing mode, making it ideal for recreational SUP paddling. The concave bottom shape towards the front enhances board directional stability.

When the wind picks up, the board can be quickly set into an adept windsurfing platform. As it attains planning speed, the step tail lifts above the water surface, effectively shortening the board by approximately 35cm. This unique feature enables the board to achieve speeds exceeding 27 knots with ease.

The bottom of the board is designed with a generous V shape. Coupled with gently rounded, tucked rails, the Windsup remains comfortable even in choppy conditions.

All sizes of the Windsup lineup are equipped with a reinforced foil box, facilitating the swift setup of the board for wind foiling sessions as well.

The Windscape is Loftsails’ dedicated bump & jump sail, designed for riders who crave easy handling, light feel, and a confident ride whether on flat water, chop, or light waves.

Its outline bridges the gap between wave and freeride/slalom designs. Above the boom, the Windscape shares DNA with the Purelip: a lightweight profile that feels crisp and reactive in the hands, making it effortless to throw around in maneuvers. Below the boom, an extended batten setup, similar in concept to the Oxygen, adds drive and tracking for blasting on a fin. While slightly less full and locked-in than the Oxygen, this lower profile is more forgiving and responsive for bump & jump-style riding.

The Windscape’s unique hybrid character gives it a wide wind range and smooth, dependable power delivery, especially useful when navigating wind holes or variable coastal conditions. A finely tuned luff curve, similar to the Purelip, ensures excellent reactivity and easy handling through jibes and transitions. For sailors looking for that balance of maneuverability and speed, it offers the best of both worlds.

Whether you’re chasing speed across flat water, weaving through gusts, or carving in light European wave conditions, the Windscape delivers with ease. It’s super light in the hands, highly controllable in strong winds, and makes every session feel smooth, fast, and fun.

Unifiber lightweight WIngfoil Harness is developed for those who value a barely-there feel.

Inspired by other wind watersports, the Wingfoil Harness improves force distribution and alleviates arm fatigue. As a result, the rider can fly longer and tack upwind more efficiently.

The continuous webbing strap angles upwards, following the wing's direction. When in flight, the Wing Harness effectively spreads the load across the lower back, allowing hands to focus on wing control. The front padding prevents any discomfort from the hook pressing against your stomach.

To simplify putting on the harness, the hook strap is equipped with a quick-release buckle. Additionally, this feature prevents the hook from sliding off when the strap is released.

The interior is lined with soft neoprene making it very comfortable, particularly when used on bare skin.

If the ankle or wrist leashes are getting in the way, the Wingfoil harness features two alternative leash attachment points.

Description:
Shaped by the challenging conditions of choppy beach breaks and unpredictable gusty onshore winds commonly encountered along the European coastline, the 2024 Xwave design has evolved to thrive in these elements.

Central to the new design is its fast rocker line. With improved acceleration and upwind mobility, Xwave can escape the shore break and swiftly reposition itself within the line-up.

New Xwave adopts a more moderate outline curve by moving the widest point of the board further forward. With significantly reduced drag, the board can maintain its momentum through deep and wide bottom turns.

When the wave conditions turn on, the Xwave can adapt and readjust its turning radius accordingly. The tail is narrowed just behind the back footstrap, coupled with a subtle tail kick. The combination allows the board to be more back-foot driven when needed through both bottom and top turns.

Xwave can be set up with a single fin or tri-fin configuration depending on conditions or personal preference.

A wave board shaped specifically for European conditions.
Along much of the European coastline, wave sailing rarely arrives on your terms. Choppy beach breaks, gusty onshore winds, and a shore break that wants to keep you in it — these are the conditions the Xwave V4 was designed around. Not ideal wave sailing. The kind you actually get. The Xwave is for intermediate to advanced wave sailors who want a board that responds to real conditions — and real decision-making in the water.

Built to Get Out and Stay Out
Before you can ride a wave, you have to reach it. A fast rocker line gives the Xwave V4 genuine acceleration off the beach and strong upwind mobility — both critical when an onshore wind is pushing you back towards the shore break. The board repositions quickly between sets, so you spend less time fighting your way out and more time choosing where to be.

Momentum Through the Turn
Moving the widest point forward shifts how the Xwave distributes its outline curve. The result is significantly reduced drag through deep, wide bottom turns — the board holds its speed into and through the arc rather than stalling at the critical moment. When conditions give you a clean wave, the Xwave carries the momentum to use it.

Back-Foot Drive When It Counts
As wave quality improves, the Xwave adapts with it. The tail narrows just behind the back footstrap, paired with a subtle tail kick. This combination shifts the board's turning character — allowing the rider to drive harder off the back foot through both bottom and top turns when the wave shape demands it. The response is direct without being nervous.

Set Up for Your Conditions
Single fin or tri-fin — the Xwave V4 accommodates both configurations. A larger centre fin suits powered, gusty days where tracking and drive matter most. Switch to a thruster setup when the conditions clean up and tighter, more pivotal turns become possible. The choice stays with the rider.

Session After Session
The Xwave V4 is for wave sailors who know that European conditions rarely deliver the textbook version of the sport — and who want a board shaped around that reality. Fast out of the shore break, composed through the turn, and responsive when the wave finally arrives.

Product name: Zypher HP & XO Sails Experience TR Rig ALU 1.0
Description:
For riders who want inflatable convenience with more drive and responsiveness, the Zypher HP inflatable Windsup and Experience TR ALU rig deliver a dependable combination that’s just as good for first steps as it is for developing your skills session after session.

The Zypher HP Windsup delivers reliable glide and balance thanks to its pintail outline and wide, confidence-inspiring nose. In SUP mode, the tail fin is placed slightly forward to improve turning response. In windsurf mode, a centre fin can be added to support upwind tracking and directional stability. The board’s Fusion Composite Dropstitch construction allows inflation up to 20 psi, adding stiffness and efficiency underfoot. A full EVA deck pad keeps you comfortable and secure, while the rear bungee net lets you carry small essentials on board

The Experience TR rig features a full-batten Dacron sail with a stable, forgiving profile. It handles light wind well, while also allowing for tuning with downhaul and outhaul when conditions pick up. The aluminium mast offers light weight and solid durability, helping early-stage riders feel more in control from the start. With colour-coded sizes, rigging markers, and a rotating boom head, it’s an intuitive and reliable choice for learning.

An inflatable setup that feels steady, safe, and ready for more.

Product name: Zypher HP & XO Sails Rookie ALU 1.0
Description:
If you’re looking for a compact, safe, and durable setup to support young or lightweight beginners in both paddling and windsurfing, the Zypher HP inflatable Windsup and XO Sails Rookie ALU rig deliver that and more. Built to handle early learning and keep up as confidence grows, this combo balances safety with performance.

The Zypher HP Windsup uses a High Pressure Fusion Composite Dropstitch build that inflates to 20 psi, making the board more rigid, responsive, and long-lasting. Its inflatable body is safer during falls or contact, especially for kids. High volume gives solid support underfoot, while a forward-positioned tail fin helps the board turn easily in SUP mode. A slot for a centre fin enhances upwind tracking while under sail. On deck, the board features directional EVA grip with added diamond zones underfoot and raised ridges near the mast base for extra hold when uphauling. The baseplate insert is protected by a traction disc, and everything packs into an ergonomic backpack.

The XO Sails Rookie rig is sized and shaped to help kids get moving confidently. Its deep lower-profile offers predictable power and stability, while the aluminium mast keeps things light and manageable. The rig is designed for simple handling, with a clear monofilm window for visibility and bright colours that make young riders easy to spot.

A reliable entry point into windsurfing and SUP for growing sailors who want gear that feels good from the start.

Description:

A capable, safe, and enjoyable setup for new windsurfers ready to build real on-the-water experience—step by step.

Product name: Zypher SL & XO Sails Rookie ALU 1.0
Description:
The Zypher SL inflatable Windsup and XO Sails Rookie ALU rig form an ideal combination for young or lightweight newcomers looking to enjoy both stand-up paddling and their first steps into windsurfing. It’s a safe, supportive setup that helps build early confidence on the water.

With its inflatable construction and generous volume, the Zypher SL Windsup offers a stable, forgiving platform that’s soft underfoot and safer in case of falls, especially important for kids and beginners. A slightly forward tail fin position makes the board more responsive in SUP mode, while an optional centre fin can be added for better upwind tracking while windsurfing. Directional EVA padding ensures good grip, and a traction disc beneath the baseplate prevents overtightening. The rear bungee net is useful for light gear or snacks on a paddle cruise. The lightweight Single Layer construction inflates to 15 psi and comes with a practical ergonomic backpack.

The XO Sails Rookie rig uses a light, balanced sail shape with a deep profile in the lower section—designed to make early steering and trimming feel natural. The included aluminium mast keeps the rig light enough for kids to lift and handle, helping them stay focused on learning rather than wrestling the sail. Bright colours and a clear monofilm window improve safety and visibility on the water.

A great setup for getting young riders on the board and enjoying the basics of SUP and sailing with ease.
